text_blocks.snippet: The Extrapyramidal Symptom Rating Scale (ESRS) is a clinician-administered assessment tool used to evaluate drug-induced movement disorders. It specifically assesses four types of movement disorders: parkinsonism, akathisia, dystonia, and tardive dyskinesia. The ESRS includes subscales for each of these movement disorders, as well as clinical global impression severity scales according to the PhenX Toolkit.
snippet_highlighted_words: a clinician-administered assessment tool used to evaluate drug-induced movement disorders

list.title: Subscales:
list.snippet: The ESRS is comprised of four subscales, each focusing on a specific type of drug-induced movement disorder.
Drug-Induced Movement Disorders: This 12-item questionnaire is rated on a 4-point scale.
Parkinsonism and Akathisia: A 7-item examination is used, rated on a 7-point scale.
Dystonia: This 10-item examination is also rated on a 7-point scale.
Dyskinesia: This 7-item examination is rated on a 7-point scale as well.

list.title: Clinical Global Impression Severity (CGI-S) Scales:
list.snippet: These scales capture the severity of tardive dyskinesia, parkinsonism, dystonia, and akathisia. Clinicians use an 8-point rating scale based on their experience.

list.title: Assessment:
list.snippet: The ESRS evaluates various aspects of these movement disorders, including tremor, orofacial dyskinesia, trunk/limb dyskinesia, and tardive dystonia.

list.title: Inter-rater Reliability:
list.snippet: The ESRS has demonstrated high inter-rater reliability in clinical studies.

list.title: Abbreviated Version:
list.snippet: An abbreviated version, the ESRS-A, is also available for assessing tardive dyskinesia.
Identify and quantify drug-induced movement disorders.
Monitor the severity of these disorders over time.
Assess the effectiveness of interventions for managing these symptoms.
Differentiate between various types of extrapyramidal symptoms.
Aid in clinical decision-making regarding medication adjustments or other treatment strategies.
